sources: Reuters reporting via millenniumpost.in/bastillepost.com (Araghchi interview with Iraq's Al Ekhbariya TV, aired Tuesday); Reuters via klse.i3investor (two Pakistani government sources on Momeni)
fault_line: Genuine peacemaker or stalling for the midterms? Iran offers to mediate Saudi-Ansar Allah while its own officials tell Reuters it is deliberately delaying US talks to wound Trump electorally.

sections.what_happened: Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi said Tehran offered to mediate between Saudi Arabia and the Ansar Allah but received no response from either side. Asked about Egypt joining Saudi military operations, Araghchi said 'any foreign intervention would complicate matters' and that Cairo had told Tehran it would 'not directly' intervene — a counterpoint to the Egypt parliament vote scheduled Oct 26 on military backing. Separately, Iran's Interior Minister Eskandar Momeni, on his second visit to Islamabad in under a week, asked Pakistan to resume its mediation role in Iran's conflict with the US (two Pakistani government sources, Reuters).
sections.what_verified: Millenniumpost + bastillepost carry the same Reuters account of the Araghchi interview; Egyptian parliament vote delay to Oct 26 corroborates the vote timeline from earlier scans.
sections.what_disputed: Araghchi's mediation offer is one-sided and self-serving: Reuters (Oct 20) reported senior Iranian officials saying Tehran is deliberately DELAYING negotiations with the US to hurt Trump in the midterms — diplomacy-as-stall tactic is a credible alternative reading.
sections.why_matters: Iran is playing mediator in Riyadh and saboteur in Washington at the same time: offering peace between Saudi and the Ansar Allah while telling Reuters it is deliberately stalling the US talks until after the midterms. The double game.
sections.context: Background: Iran's mediation diplomacy — Araghchi offered to mediate Saudi-Ansar Allah talks (no answer); Egypt told Tehran it will NOT directly intervene; Iran's interior minister in Islamabad asked Pakistan to resume mediation role
